text.p: Base metals soared, led by nickel and zinc. Wheat closed firmer, crude was slightly off and gold ended slightly down after hitting a two-month high. The CRB index closed up 1.19 points at 243.60.
A sharp rise in base metal prices was inspired by strong gains in the jittery nickel market and an influx of speculative interest.
Zinc peaked at a 4-1/2 year high after breaching a key resistance level, while aluminium hit a near one-year high and copper approached last week's nine month high.

Nickel prices led the way, shooting up to a 9-1/2 month high of $8,320 per tonne on weekend news that workers at Russia's huge Norilsk complex had adopted a strike plan. It settled near its highs at $8,310, a gain of $240 from Friday's kerb close. Traders said it was aiming at $8,400 next.
Norilsk management said they could not meet union demands for repayment of salary arrears, but predicted workers would not stop production fully.
The LME's upward momentum was extended in the afternoon with U.S. funds coming onto the scene, attracted by some metals' proximity to technical break out points, traders and analysts said.
Copper regained the $2,400 level and touched last week's high trade of $2,415 before settling at $2,408, a gain of $30 from Friday's close.
Aluminium posted an even stronger technical close of $1,690, a gain of $36 and the highest since March 21, 1996.
Zinc also sped higher, punching briefly to a 4-1/2 year high when it touched $1,240. It ended just below at $1,239, a gain of $21 on the day.
The other base metals absorbed the positive tone, although their gains were less notable.
Lead was slightly firmer at $702, up $4, while tin racked up $70 to end at $5,860.

Wheat closed steady to five cents higher per bushel. Prices were underpinned by strong gains in soybean futures, traders said, although large supplies of world wheat limited gains. Pit sources said Cargill Inc sold 6.0 million bushels July on the day. March wheat closed unchanged at $3.73 per bushel.

April crude was 10 cents weaker at $20.20 per barrel in late trading after dipping below $20 for the first time in eight months but avoiding an undertow of sell stops and bobbing back above that level.

COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended mostly lower Monday, but not before gold made a new two-month high. COMEX April gold ended down $1.30 an ounce at $364.00, after seeing a 366.00-363.50 range, with estimated total volume for the gold strip at 25,000 lots. In the bullion market, spot gold closed quoted $361.70/20, compared with the London Monday afternoon fix at $362.15, and the New York close Friday around $363.50/00.

CSCE world sugar futures ended lower Monday, after a choppy but high volume session which cast doubt on how much momentum remains in the six-week-old rally, traders said. CSCE May sugar ended down 0.13 cent at 10.84 cents a pound, after seeing an 11.08-10.68 cent range. The May/July backwardation ended around 0.21 cent down from 0.25 cent Friday.
